facts.shortSummary: Kenzo retrieves a magical pearl from the dead roper while the party orients itself in the ruined dwarven market.
facts.longSummary: The session opens moments after the roper's defeat, with Inakara and her companions watching from the passage. The party wants to recover Riswynn's family heirloom and find a route toward Raven's Hold across the valley. Seeker senses valuable stone to the south and below, near the edge of his 300-foot range. Kenzo identifies the roper as an underground ambush predator and uses an old mage's staff to pry a pearl from its acidic remains, partly dissolving the staff. Delwath detects transmutation magic; Kenzo passes the pearl to Riswynn for ritual identification. An early suggestion to rest has not yet been carried out.

location.context: Ruined marketplace, immediately after the roper battle.

npcs.name: Inakara
npcs.notes: Named later in this session; she is the same dwarf-like woman watching the party here.

items.notes: Riswynn's sought family heirloom, not yet recovered.

facts.shortSummary: The party finds hobgoblin graffiti, rests in the tavern, and scouts the corrupted valley outside.
facts.longSummary: The ruined tavern contains faded graffiti of a hand with three burned, bony fingers and unreadable writing; Wellby recognizes the symbol as a hobgoblin battle banner his people have fled. The market was deliberately sacked, while the tavern appears to have been reused, but the occupants' identities and the circumstances of the dwarves' flight remain unclear. Riswynn identifies the pearl's ability to restore spellcasting energy. About half an hour has passed before the group takes a short rest in the tavern; Seeker attunes to the Pearl of Power, restores a second-level spell slot, and feels it gathering energy from the land. Afterward, in mid-afternoon, Wellby peers through the main entrance at a hazy valley with black, slimy cattails, thorny plants, dead trees, and a dark, almost bloody river. He sees no movement, returns, and the party chooses to seek the vault.

location.context: Tavern and ruined market, with a brief scout to the nearby main entrance.

npcs.name: Eberk Brawnanvil
npcs.notes: Riswynn's great-uncle drew the imperfect map from old memories and would not discuss the final flight.

items.notes: Riswynn identifies it; Seeker attunes and uses it during the rest.

items.name: Hobgoblin hand graffiti
items.notes: Faded battle-banner symbol; the accompanying writing is not deciphered.

items.name: Eberk's map
items.notes: Useful but imperfect recollection of the outpost.

facts.shortSummary: Riswynn bargains for passage while the others intimidate Inakara with displays of magic.
facts.longSummary: Inakara insists the roper bargain bought safe passage out, not freedom to explore her kingdom, and speaks with the party in broken Dwarvish. Kenzo's soul sight shows that she fears the party and has considerable strength and magic; most of her attendants seem emotionally flat, while one better-equipped follower appears anxious and angry. Riswynn offers a small share of any treasure, and Inakara becomes eager when the mirror doors are mentioned. Seeker makes his fingers seem to stretch like tentacles, Kenzo strikes his staff with a tremor and flaring light, and Delwath conjures a sword crackling with green flame. Inakara backs away and lets them pass, promising to watch and threatening that their brains may be eaten and their bodies thrown to the blind ones.

location.context: Passage between the market and the inhabited cavern.

npcs.name: Inakara
npcs.notes: Blocks exploration, then allows passage after the bargain and intimidation.

items.name: Pearl of Power
items.notes: Discussed as a possible gift, but Seeker explicitly refuses to give it away.

facts.shortSummary: The party reaches the vault entrance, discusses Kenzo's mind-flayer vision, and detects an invisible follower.
facts.longSummary: Moving north past the pools, the party reaches a circular chamber with a dwarf statue bearing a family resemblance to Riswynn. Kenzo describes a vision or memory not his own of the dwarf-like residents associated with a tall, tentacle-mouthed creature, suggesting a mind-flayer connection without establishing that one is nearby. The party takes the southeast passage down beneath the market to an antechamber with three polished brass doors, two armored statues, and a low divider that once supported bars and a gate. Wellby hears an invisible follower, runs back with his torch, and calls for a conversation. Muttering in broken Dwarvish and retreating footsteps suggest Inakara; the follower stays roughly 50–60 feet away while the party returns to the doors.

location.context: Route north around the pools, through the statue chamber, and southeast down to the vault antechamber.

npcs.name: Inakara
npcs.notes: Probable invisible follower, inferred from the voice and context.

npcs.name: Mind flayer in Kenzo's vision
npcs.notes: Seen in a recalled vision or memory; no living mind flayer is encountered.

facts.shortSummary: Seeker and Riswynn use keys visible in the brass reflections to open the vault.
facts.longSummary: Wellby thoroughly checks the antechamber and finds no mechanical traps. Seeker notices necklaces on the statues' reflections in the brass doors, although none is visible on the statues themselves or in an ordinary mirror; Riswynn can see them too, while the others cannot. Keeping their eyes on the reflections, the two dwarves feel the keys and lift them together, making physical keys and two keyholes appear. They turn both keys through a full circle; light from the side doors joins at the middle door, which opens onto a descending corridor. The party proceeds together, with Wellby listening at the rear; the invisible watcher appears to balk at the bright light.

location.context: Vault antechamber and the short corridor beyond the opened central door.

npcs.name: Inakara
npcs.notes: Probable invisible watcher kept back by the bright doorway.

items.name: Mirror doors
items.notes: Opened by the two dwarves using the reflected keys.

items.name: Reflected keys
items.notes: Two keys removed from the statues and used in the side doors.

facts.shortSummary: Riswynn recovers her ancestral shield among the remains of five dwarves, a dead mind flayer, and surviving treasure.
facts.longSummary: In the dusty vault, four dwarven skeletons lie carefully arranged and a fifth rests slumped against the wall with a pristine rune-covered warhammer. A smashed mind-flayer skull lies by the inner iron doors. Riswynn recognizes her family's shield, whose value lies in preserving ancestral stories, and reserves it for return to her people. Seeker recognizes thunderous-force and stoneworking resonances in the hammer's runes and respectfully takes it after discussing dwarven traditions of returning relics to their clans. Wellby opens a chest containing six bottles marked three 'life,' two 'strength,' and one 'health,' plus two crystal globes; Kenzo opens another holding fourteen silver and four gold trade bars stamped with the Brawnanvil crest. The arrangement suggests a mortally wounded dwarf laid the other four to rest after the old battle. Riswynn agrees to share the other treasure and carries the bars while the party prepares to examine the inner room.

location.context: Ancient vault beyond the mirror doors.

npcs.notes: Five long-dead dwarves; their arrangement suggests one outlived the others briefly.

facts.shortSummary: Delwath scouts a deliberately blocked tunnel and returns with adamantine from a deep mine shaft.
facts.longSummary: The inner vault is ruined, with a non-dwarven tunnel blocked by rubble to the west. Seeker uses stone magic to open a small gap and finds hammer marks suggesting a deliberate collapse; the tunnel beyond looks as if a directed earthquake formed it. The party infers that the ancient mind flayer entered this way and a defender blocked the breach. Delwath casts Invisibility and scouts several hundred feet down the steep passage, finding no tracks or recent disturbance. It ends at a roughly fifteen-foot-wide vertical mine shaft extending beyond his sight above and below. Using Mage Hand and a hammer, he chips off a metal-bearing sample, choosing to catch it and let the hammer fall; he hears no impact. He returns and Seeker identifies adamantine. This spot lies beyond the earlier stone-sense range, so the same ore may be accessible higher in the mine, but the exact earlier source is not located.

location.context: Ruined inner vault, breached western tunnel, and deep mine shaft; Delwath returns to the vault.

items.name: Adamantine sample
items.notes: Retrieved by Delwath and identified by Seeker.

items.name: Mundane hammer
items.notes: Dropped into the shaft while Mage Hand catches the ore sample; no impact heard.

items.name: Shatterstorm
items.notes: Carried by Seeker; suspected connection to the ancient cave-in remains an inference.

facts.shortSummary: After securing the vault, the party pays Inakara in silver to guide them to a locked tunnel toward Raven's Hold.
facts.longSummary: The two crystal globes are identified as driftglobes that provide light and, once per day, daylight; Kenzo takes one. Seeker reseals the rubble, the party pays respects to the dead, and turning the mirror-door keys back extinguishes the light and restores the keys to the statues' reflections. Inakara reappears to demand treasure. The party gives her two silver bars and promises three more for guidance; she will take them to a tunnel but refuses to lead them through it and admits she has never passed its locked bars. Naming herself, she claims the coming brain eaters will spare her and kill the party. She guides them by the statue chamber and shadowy halls, warns against an unidentified 'white dangling' danger to the north, and reaches a rusty chained gate beneath the main entrance. Beyond it a tunnel leads east. She threatens to point the party out to the newcomers, then vanishes.

location.context: Return from the vault through the statue chamber and halls to the barred tunnel below the main entrance.

npcs.name: Inakara
npcs.notes: Takes silver for guidance, refuses to go through the gate, and makes threatening claims about the future.

items.name: Dwarven Driftglobe

items.name: Brawnanvil trade bars

items.name: Mirror doors
items.notes: Closed again; the keys vanish from the locks and return in reflection.

items.notes: Rusty bars secured with a padlock and chain across the eastbound tunnel.

facts.shortSummary: Inakara claims she is preparing for the mind flayers, and the party stops at the locked gate with the larger threat unresolved.
facts.longSummary: The table revisits questions asked before Inakara's departure and clarifies payment on reaching the tunnel. Inakara dismisses the sightless ones as powerless figures who sit, moan, and lurk in shadows, insisting she does everything. When the party names mind flayers, she says they are coming and that she is preparing the way and keeping the entrance clear; she asks for help clearing other passages but refuses their secrets. Kenzo senses fear and doubts her offer to sell more information. Play ends before the party opens the rusty gate. In the discussion afterward, they distinguish the old corpse, Kenzo's vision, and Inakara's claims from speculation about an army or a link to the portal and poisoned water. Their intended purpose remains reconnaissance and reporting to Candrosa and the Dunmari, with retreat still possible.

location.context: Locked lower gate; includes questions added retrospectively to the same conversation and discussion after play stops.
